questions.q: What is `Object.extendsObject()` in ServiceNow's class pattern?
options: The real ServiceNow API for setting up prototype-based inheritance between two classes
A method for copying a GlideRecord into a new table
A deprecated API that was replaced by a native `extends` keyword
A client-side-only function with no server-side equivalent
questions.explain: Object.extendsObject(ParentClass, { ...child methods... }) is the real API, and its result becomes the child class's prototype.

options: Explicitly calls the parent class's constructor with `this` set to the current child instance — the real "calling super"
Deletes the parent class from memory
Creates a second, separate instance of IncidentUtils
Has no effect; it's leftover code that can be safely removed
questions.explain: There's no super() keyword in this pattern — you explicitly reach into the parent's prototype and call its initialize with this bound to the child instance.

questions.q: In `PriorityIncidentUtils.prototype = Object.extendsObject(IncidentUtils, { ... })`, what does the resulting `PriorityIncidentUtils` have access to?
options: Every method IncidentUtils had (like isHighPriority and getOpenDurationHours), plus its own new methods like needsEscalation
Only the methods explicitly listed in the second argument, with no access to IncidentUtils' methods at all
Only the type property from IncidentUtils
Nothing from IncidentUtils unless each method is manually copied over line by line
questions.explain: Object.extendsObject merges the parent's prototype in, so the child inherits every parent method automatically, on top of its own.

questions.q: A developer is deciding whether PriorityIncidentUtils should extend IncidentUtils or be a brand-new, unrelated class. What's the real test, per this lesson?
options: Whether PriorityIncidentUtils genuinely IS A more specific version of IncidentUtils that should inherit most of its behavior
Whether both classes happen to reference the same table
Whether both classes were written by the same developer
Whether the two class names start with the same word
questions.explain: The real test is the IS-A relationship — sharing a table is not enough reason to force an inheritance relationship.

questions.q: Two Script Includes both work with the Incident table: one formats incident numbers for a report, the other routes incidents to assignment groups. Per this lesson, why is forcing one to extend the other a mistake?
options: Neither IS A more specific version of the other, so the inheritance would be a false dependency that lets an unrelated change break the other class
ServiceNow technically prevents two classes from ever referencing the same table
Extending a class always doubles its memory footprint
Script Includes can only extend classes defined in the global scope
questions.explain: Working with the same table isn't a real parent-child relationship — forcing one anyway creates a false dependency between unrelated logic.
